name: Dumpas
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Boutin, Michael E. & Inka Pekkanen (eds.). 1993. Phonological descriptions of Sabah languages: studies from ten languages. Sabah Museum Monograph 4. (title page / contents)
sources.note: Not applicable: the ten languages are Bonggi, Ida'an, Kadazan/Dusun, Kalabuan, Kimaragang, Labuk-Kinabatangan Kadazan, Lotud, Tagal, Tatana, Tombonuwo -- no Dumpas chapter.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: a comprehensive classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing; Dumpas lexical items (taken from Lobel 2016) appear only in lexical-innovation tables.

sources.citation: OLAC: Resources in and about the Dumpas language [dmv] (snapshot 2025-11-17); SIL Language & Culture Archives search for [dmv] (the Internet Archive 2015) and record 79990
sources.note: Bibliographic: the only archived items for Dumpas are Hurlbut 1976 (word list) and King 1984; no phonology or grammar exists in SIL's archive listing.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa (sec. 11.4.4 'Dumpas', pp. 396-398). hdl:10125/101972
sources.note: Nothing for Dumpas. Sec. 11.4.4 is subgrouping only (Dumpas a close relative of Sungai Karamuak/Sukang, Paitanic features by contact); Dumpas functor forms cited without accent marks.

sources.citation: Kroeger, Paul. 1996. Asu vs. Tasu: on the origins of Dusunic moveable t-. In Collins (ed.), Language and Oral Traditions in Borneo (BRC Proceedings 2) [prepublication draft].
sources.note: Nothing on stress; fn. 12 states 'The only Dumpas data immediately available comes from Hurlbut's 1976 wordlist.'
sources.venue: Language and Oral Traditions in Borneo (BRC Proceedings 2) [prepublication draft]

sources.citation: King, Julie K. 1984. The Dumpas language. In Julie K. King & John Wayne King (eds.), Languages of Sabah: a survey report, 231-235. Pacific Linguistics C-78. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-C78.231
sources.note: Nothing. Survey chapter: location (Perancangan LS), population, lexicostatistics, intelligibility testing, Paitanic-vs-Dusunic classification. The entire PL C-78 volume (incl. Smith 1984, pp. 1-49) contains no occurrence of 'stress', 'accent' or 'penult'.
sources.venue: Languages of Sabah: a survey report

sources.citation: Smith, Kenneth D. 1984. The languages of Sabah: a tentative lexicostatistical classification. In King & King (eds.), Languages of Sabah: a survey report, 1-49. Pacific Linguistics C-78.
sources.note: Nothing; lexicostatistical classification only (Dumpas placed in Dusunic, sec. 2.3.9.4.2).
sources.venue: Languages of Sabah: a survey report

sources.citation: Hurlbut, Hope M. (compiler). 1976. Dumpas Word List - Sabah, E. Malaysia. 10 pp. (374-item word list with English gloss; p.10 'Comments on Orthography of Dumpas Word List'). SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 79990 (draft, posted as is).
sources.note: Nothing. Typed list in government (Kadazan) orthography without stress/accent marks; p.10 notes cover light 'l', four vowels a i o u, and glottal stop ('so rare.. only 4 words'); no mention of stress, accent or syllables.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2016. North Borneo Sourcebook: vocabularies and functors. (PALI Language Texts: Southeast Asia.) Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. 288 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only modern first-hand Dumpas data (Lobel's own fieldwork); the introduction / 'Language Information' (pp. 1-66) and transcription conventions may mark or remark on stress for the Dusunic wordlists including Dumpas. Everything else that exists has been read and is silent.
